sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205], but the path was a step change, not a smooth climb.
Revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021 [D183][D230], then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores, with the pandemic shifting category and channel mix [P51].
The recent decline reflects a 2.6% comparable sales decrease in FY2025, driven by a 2.2% drop in traffic and a 0.4% drop in average transaction [P14].
Merchandise sales are 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 [D465] and subtracted 2.0pp from growth that year [D467].
Food & beverage is the largest growing category at 23.0% of revenue [D506], adding 0.3pp in FY2025 [D508], while apparel fell 4.7% and subtracted 0.7pp [D564][D565].
The filings attribute the discretionary weakness to sales declines in Apparel & Accessories, Hardlines and Home Furnishings & Decor, partly offset by Frequency categories [P30].
Operating income fell 8.1% in FY2025 against a 1.7% revenue decline [D417][D416], so there was no operating leverage; operating income compounded at only 0.6% over the window [F207].
Diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against net income's 3.4% [F210][F208], as diluted shares fell from 582.5 million to 455.6 million [X107][X116].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025 [F34], below the 5.6% window median [D590] and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high [D589].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp [D429], with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D440][D441].
Gross margin fell to 27.9% from 28.2% on the net impact of several items the filing lists without quantifying [P12].
The SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because of a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit; excluding it, the adjusted rate rose to 20.9% on sales deleverage [P11].
The effective tax rate rose to 22.3% from 22.2% on global minimum taxes and share-based compensation expense [P9][D403].
Operating cash flow was $6.56 billion and free cash flow $2.84 billion in FY2025 [F84][F104], a 2.7% FCF margin against the 4.5% window median [D401][D596].
Free cash flow covered net income only 0.77x [D405], below the 1.01x window median [D599] and the 0.93x peer median [D615].
The operating cash flow decline reflects lower net earnings plus lower accounts payable leverage and inventory purchases [P7].
Capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion, or 3.6% of revenue [D423][F94][D400], and was 1.19x D&A [D406].
Net debt was $4.30 billion, or 4.1% of revenue [D410][D411], a larger net debt burden than the retail peer median of -3.5% net cash, though it ranks at the 50th percentile of six peers [D613][D612].
Cash and investments reached $10.1 billion against $14.4 billion of debt [D408][D409], and the current ratio was 0.94x [F184].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow [D412][D413], with buybacks cut to $408 million [X126].
Return on average equity was 24.0% [D415], below the 28.6% peer median and the 40th percentile of five peers [D617][D616].
Revenue has now fallen three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F7][F8][F9][F10], a persistent top-line erosion [R1].
The current ratio sits at 0.94x [F184], below 1.0x and at the window median [D602], leaving little liquidity cushion [R2].
Operating margin has slipped two years in a row, 0.4pp in total [F32][F33][F34][R4], consistent with the deleverage the filing describes [P11].
The FY2022 buyback figure was later restated to $2.65 billion from $2.83 billion [R5][X123]; the pack uses the first-reported value, so capital-return ratios for that year are approximate.
If operating margin in the FY2026 10-K falls below the 4.9% FY2025 level [F34], the two-year slide becomes a structural margin problem rather than a cyclical one.
If free cash flow margin stays below the 4.5% window median [D596], the 86.8% payout of FCF [D413] becomes harder to sustain.

Capex guidance of about $5 billion for FY2026 [P4] against FY2025's $3.73 billion [F94] would lift capex well above FY2025's 3.6% of revenue [D400] if sales hold at $104.8 billion [F10], testing the cash conversion trend.
